title: High-dose ifosfamide for recurrent Ewing sarcoma or relapsed osteosarcoma
context_label: Recurrent or primary refractory Ewing sarcoma, or relapsed osteosarcoma
indication_text: Recurrent or primary refractory Ewing sarcoma, or relapsed osteosarcoma
purpose: High-dose ifosfamide aims to control previously treated sarcoma and can sometimes make further local treatment possible. The specialist team weighs potential tumour shrinkage against substantial bone-marrow, brain, kidney and bladder risks.
schedule_label: Five consecutive 24-hour ifosfamide infusions; every 21 days, maximum 4 cycles
schedule_summary: Ifosfamide 3,000 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours on each of days 1–5, giving five consecutive 24-hour infusions. Repeat every 21 days for a maximum of four cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity stops treatment sooner. Mesna starts before the first infusion, continues throughout the five-day treatment and includes a final dose on day 6 after the last ifosfamide infusion.
administration_text: The five 24-hour ifosfamide infusions total 120 hours at the full reference schedule. Mesna 400 mg/m² is given one hour before the first ifosfamide dose, then 3,000 mg/m² over each 24 hours alongside ifosfamide, with a final 800 mg/m² intravenous dose on day 6 after completion. Hydration continues for 24 hours after ifosfamide ends. Actual bag changes, finish times and any alternative final mesna route require pharmacy confirmation.
monitoring_summary: Use the individual test cards below: each test has its own purpose and timing. Safety tests and tumour-response assessment answer different questions.

agents.name: Ifosfamide
agents.mechanism: A liver-activated medicine damages genetic material
agents.explanation: The liver converts ifosfamide into active compounds that crosslink DNA, the genetic material, preventing normal cell division. Other breakdown products can damage the bladder, kidneys or brain. Mesna reduces bladder injury; it does not prevent kidney injury or brain toxicity.
agents.watch: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness, seizures, blood in urine or reduced urine needs immediate assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, hair loss and fatigue
Brain toxicity, called encephalopathy: confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations or seizures; may be severe
Kidney tubular injury, electrolyte loss and reduced kidney function, which may persist
Bladder inflammation and bleeding despite protective mesna; report blood or pain when passing urine
Possible heart or lung injury, allergic reactions, fertility and pregnancy harm, and later cancers

anatomy: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures needs immediate assessment.
Report ulcers, painful swallowing or difficulty eating and drinking early.
New breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, faintness or swelling needs urgent assessment.
Report reduced urine or inability to drink. Kidney damage and electrolyte losses may need extra tests.
Report blood or pain when passing urine immediately. Mesna reduces bladder injury but does not remove all risk.
Fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding requires immediate oncology advice.
Use prescribed anti-sickness support; report persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea or difficulty drinking.
Hair and skin changes may occur. Report line-site pain, burning, swelling or a severe rash immediately.

monitoring_schedule.note: The national regimen, product information and individual clinical plan may require different tests. Your treating team writes the actual dates and reviews results before treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess infection risk, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each 21-day cycle; extra testing follows fever, bleeding or abnormal results. Ifosfamide product information additionally specifies counts before each administration and appropriate intervals afterwards; the team reconciles the daily course monitoring.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess drug handling and detect organ injury.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each cycle. Kidney filtration and tubular function also need assessment during and after ifosfamide, with timing intensified for abnormal results or symptoms.

monitoring_test_details.label: Neurological assessment
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before EVERY ifosfamide dose and urgently for new confusion, sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine checks for blood
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before each ifosfamide dose and every 8 hours on treatment days; report blood or urinary pain immediately.

monitoring_test_details.label: Fluid balance and weight
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect low urine output, fluid retention and dehydration.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Monitor fluid balance during treatment and record weight daily. Prescribed hydration begins before ifosfamide and continues for 24 hours after the final ifosfamide infusion ends.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour, symptom and function review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before continuation at the specialist-set review points; scan timing depends on the individual Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma treatment plan.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm the five-day infusion admission, mesna, hydration, daily bag changes, white-cell growth-factor support and anti-sickness prescription. Review previous ifosfamide neurological problems and interacting medicines, including aprepitant. This high-dose regimen has high nausea/vomiting risk and requires white-cell growth-factor support. Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential but do not remove kidney or brain toxicity. The anti-sickness plan needs specific interaction review and coverage for treatment and delayed symptoms.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Never change pump settings or disconnect an infusion yourself.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Obtain written contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue after the final dose. Different medicines have different requirements. Contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible. Children and young people need age-appropriate information, assent and the applicable parent or guardian consent process.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: The specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team considers prior treatment, sites of disease, whether surgery or radiotherapy could help, clinical trials, symptoms and your priorities. These options have different roles in Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma. Rehabilitation and symptom-focused care can accompany anticancer treatment at any stage.

evidence.title: High-dose ifosfamide cohorts in Ewing sarcoma and relapsed osteosarcoma
evidence.summary: Small Ewing sarcoma and retrospective osteosarcoma studies reported tumour shrinkage in some patients. Severe blood-count toxicity was frequent in the Ewing study. These studies support a carefully selected disease-control discussion but cannot establish a comparative survival benefit.
evidence.intro: Small Ewing sarcoma and retrospective osteosarcoma studies reported tumour shrinkage in some patients. Severe blood-count toxicity was frequent in the Ewing study. These studies support a carefully selected disease-control discussion but cannot establish a comparative survival benefit.
evidence.caveat: Ewing and osteosarcoma results come from different uncontrolled populations and must not be combined or used to rank regimens. Surgery and patient selection affect the osteosarcoma survival figures. The current national course maximum remains four cycles.
evidence.interpretation: Ewing and osteosarcoma results come from different uncontrolled populations and must not be combined or used to rank regimens. Surgery and patient selection affect the osteosarcoma survival figures. The current national course maximum remains four cycles.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can treatment restart when a blood test improves?
questions.a: Only when the treating team confirms a new plan. A previous serious reaction, stopped medicine or required protective treatment still matters.
